text:
sophie: FYI escalated ticket from Acme Corp — customer seeing intermittent 502s and timeouts against hosted inference endpoint since ~06:12 UTC. I repro locally from eu-west via curl and we see TLS handshake timeouts plus gateway 502s.

ashok: Looking. which endpoint + customer org id?

sophie: org=acme, endpoint = /v1/generate (hosted-us-east). Quick repro curl: 
```
curl -v https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer xxxxx' -d '{"prompt":"hi"}' --max-time 15
* TCP_NODELAY set
* Connected to api.redwood.example (54.23.12.7) port 443 (#0)
* TLS handshake timeout
* Closing connection 0
curl: (28) Operation timed out after 15001 milliseconds with 0 bytes received
```

sophie: Gateway logs (edge-node-14) around 06:12: 
```
[06:12:07] warn tls: handshake timeout after 10000ms, client_ip=203.0.113.44, route=/v1/generate
[06:12:07] error gateway: upstream returned 502, upstream_err="tls: remote error: handshake failure"
```

maria: Any DNS resolver rotations or TTL churn reported? That pattern looks like backends are flipping under a cert rotation.

sophie: I pulled resolver logs — there is a resolver rotation event at 06:11:55 UTC that shuffled resolver pool for edge-node-14. dig output from a repro host: 
```
; <<>> DiG 9.11.3 <<>> api.redwood.example A +short +tries=1 +time=2 @127.0.0.1
54.23.12.7
54.23.12.8
```

ashok: Interesting — infra bot shows cert rolling at 06:10:50 for redwood-edge-v2 (canary rolling 8% then 30%). If resolver rotation returned a backend IP that hadn't completed cert rollout, we can see handshake failures.

infra-bot: deploy-redwood-edge-v2 cert-rotation started at 2024-08-15T06:10:50Z, batch=1/12, status=rolling

leo: Customer traffic path? Some customers hit mixed pools (canary + stable) depending on resolver pick. If DNS rotation and cert rotation overlap, SNI/chain mismatch is possible.

maria: Agreed. Short repro to validate: run openssl s_client to the problematic IP and check cert chain and SNI: 
```
openssl s_client -connect 54.23.12.7:443 -servername api.redwood.example -timeout 5
```
If handshake hangs or cert CN mismatch -> evidence.

sophie: Ran that against 54.23.12.7 at 06:13:12: got no cert, connection reset. Against .8 it worked and returned expected cert.

ashok: Root cause hypothesis: overlapping resolver rotation + canary cert rollout created a window where some resolver answers pointed clients at nodes that still had old certs or partially applied chains -> TLS handshake failures -> gateway returns 502.

ashok: Mitigations in priority order:
1) temporarily pause cert canary rollout (rollback to stable) for edge-v2 until resolver rotation stabilizes.
2) Add a short cooldown on resolver pool rotation when cert-rotation events are in-flight.
3) Short-term routing fallback: route customer traffic to stable pool explicitly (support can toggle route).

sophie: I paused the canary for edge-v2 at 06:20 and routed acme -> stable-pool; customer reports 90% drop in 502s after 06:25.

maria: Please capture pcap/tcpdump for one of the failing sessions for postmortem: 
`sudo tcpdump -n -s 0 -w /tmp/handshake-acme.pcap host 203.0.113.44 and port 443`
Also collect resolver/pool logs: `/var/log/resolver/pool.log` lines around 06:10-06:15.

leo: I'll coordinate with support-ops to notify the customer about a temporary mitigation and that we're doing a root cause analysis.

support-ops: Noted — opened SEV-1254 for customer communication. Will schedule RCA once packs and pcaps are uploaded.

sophie: Uploaded pcap + edge logs to 1password share and attached to the ticket.

ashok: Next steps: infra will add an interlock in the rollout pipeline to prevent overlapping resolver rotations and cert canary batches. I'll open infra task and link here.

maria: Thanks — marking this as "mitigated" for now. We'll track RCA items: rollout interlock, resolver cooldown, and customer routing control as follow-ups.

sophie: Thanks team :thumbsup: — keep me posted if you need more traces.
